sheet-1.description: This part is the lower half of the title sheet: a 50 feet to an inch map of the blocks on either side of South Broad Street between 5th Street and 7th Street, reaching east to South Chestnut Street. The upper half of the sheet, holding the key map of the town at about 500 feet to an inch, the street index, the list of specials and the water and fire department notes, is not part of this georeferenced area. Fifth Street, drawn 120 feet wide with a private railroad along it, runs across the top; 6th Street is 60 feet wide east of Broad and narrower (30 feet) and slightly offset to the west; 7th Street closes the map at the bottom. Blocks 30 and 31, east of Broad, are residential, with frame dwellings, private garages, a storage building and chicken coops; most houses are two storeys. West of Broad, block 70 carries a few dwellings and garages along 5th and 6th streets, and block 74 to the south is shown empty. Much of the area is still open lots, especially the southern half of block 30 and the middle of block 31, which reflects the thin development of the south side of Florence in 1930. Lot lines, house numbers and street widths are drawn throughout, and the margins refer to sheet 2 to the north, sheet 10 to the west and sheet 11 to the east.
notes: 7th Street is Wilbur Henry Drive in OpenStreetMap.
Upper half of the sheet (key map at about 500 ft to an inch, index, water and fire notes) is masked out.
5th Street junctions were left out: the 120 ft street carries a private railroad and its modern centre lies about 6 m from the drawn one (with them the fit was 2.4 m RMSE, without 0.1 m).

Title sheet: key map (500 ft, not configured), index and water/fire notes in the upper half; lower half is a 50 ft map of W/E 5th to 7th St between S Broad and S Chestnut (blocks 30, 31, 70, 74). One part (the lower map). W/E 5th St junctions left out (railroad in street, 6 m off).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the centre of Florence on either side of Broad Street, from Front Street south to 5th Street, with South Chestnut Street along the east edge. The blocks west of Broad (blocks 21, 22, 23 and 63, with the Front Street frontage of block 20) and east of it (blocks 25 and 26, and the large block 24) are drawn at 50 feet to an inch. North of Front Street only the corner of North Broad Street is shown, with stores and a shed; the rest of that side is marked vacant to the river. The Front Street and Broad Street frontages are the town's commercial core: stores, a bakery with an oven, a club, offices and the post office at the corner of East Front and Broad. West of Broad between 2nd and 3rd streets stand the Florence M.E. Church, the American Legion Post No. 194 in a concrete block building, and the O.U.A.M. Lodge Halls. East of Broad the blocks between Front and 3rd streets are lined with frame dwellings and outbuildings. Block 24, between East 3rd and East 5th streets, is almost empty apart from a hall and two dwellings. South of West 4th Street, west of Broad, stands a Public Service Corporation gas valve house. Street widths are lettered in the margins: Front Street 100 feet, 2nd, 3rd and 4th streets 60 feet, 5th Street 120 feet, with 20 foot alleys through the blocks. The adjoining sheets are numbered 3 to the west, 10 to the southwest and 11 to the east.
notes: Street names unchanged today except that the numbered streets carry West and East prefixes in OpenStreetMap.
Front Street is drawn 100 ft wide and 5th Street 120 ft wide.
W/E Front to E 5th St, S Broad and S Chestnut (blocks 20-26, 54, 63). 50 ft. One part.

sheet-3-1.description: Sheet 3, part 1, shows the blocks west of the town centre of Florence from West Front Street south to West 4th Street, between South Summer Street at the left and South Spring Street, with the edge of block 20 at the top left beside the Delaware River. Blocks 18 and 19 lie to the left and 21 and 22 to the right of South Spring Street, with blocks 55 and 23 below West 3rd Street. The main feature is the Florence Public School No. 1 in block 18, a large brick building with an auditorium and stage, steam heated and electrically lit. Beside it stand the First National Bank on West Front Street and rows of frame dwellings along West Front, West 2nd and West 3rd streets. On the right St. Stephens Episcopal Church stands in block 21, with a garage, an auto accessories shop and a hotel facing West Front Street, and the fire house of the Volunteer Fire Company No. 1 and the police department in block 22. Block 55 holds greenhouses at its lower left. Much of block 19 is vacant. Street widths are lettered at the margins: West Front Street is 100 feet and the numbered streets 60 feet, with 20 foot alleys. The upper right of the sheet is a separate inset, block 1, behind a heavy line; it is not part of this part. A turned north arrow and compass rose stand at the right edge, and the adjoining sheets are numbered 4, 2 and 10.
notes: Printed S. Summer, S. Spring and W. Front are Summer Street, Spring Street and West Front Street in OpenStreetMap; the numbered streets carry West prefixes there.
Delaware Av. at the top left is Riverview Avenue today.
Block 20 at the top left is part of this part; the inset at the top right (block 1) is a separate part left unplaced.
Spring Street / West Front Street and Summer Street / West Front Street were not detected; placement rests on the other six junctions.

W Front to W 4th St, S Summer and S Spring (blocks 18-23, 55); block 20 by the Delaware River and N Summer at top left. 50 ft. Part 2: inset at top right behind a heavy line, block 1 (no exposure all round, by the river near the foundry per the key map). Configured as sheet-3-1.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: block 1 north of West Front Street beside the foundry works, about 225 ft from Front St (ice house, dwellings, sheds) (no street junction; no exposure on every side; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-7 if a shared building can be matched).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the north-west quarter of Florence, from West Delaware Avenue on the Delaware River south to West 4th Street, between North Church Street at the left and North and South Summer Street at the right. The upper left holds blocks 56 and 112 on either side of North Laurel Avenue: rows of small double frame dwellings, with five pink-coloured brick pairs in block 56, and the margin is marked no exposure to the north. West Delaware Avenue runs on a diagonal across the upper right along the river, with block 113 above it and block 114 between it and West Front Street; the Mohican Boat Club house stands on the avenue beside a storage shed and a small coloured building near the river. Below West Front Street the sheet is mainly dwellings with rear sheds: block 14 on the left with an auto repair shop, block 16 on the right with a row of narrow buildings filled blue and a row of dwellings, block 17, block 15 and then blocks 79 and 54 along West 4th Street. Water pipes of 6 inch size and dry hydrants are drawn along the streets. Street widths are lettered: West Front Street 100 feet, the other streets 60 feet, with 20 foot alleys and 35 foot half widths on Church Street. A scale bar and the Sanborn compass rose, turned so north is toward the upper left, are on the sheet. Adjoining sheets are numbered 3, 5 and 10.
notes: West Delaware Avenue is Riverview Avenue in OpenStreetMap; North Laurel Avenue is Laurel Avenue; the Winter, Summer and Church streets drop the printed North/South prefix.
Church Street runs on a different bearing in the upper left from the lower left, so the left-hand blocks step westward down the sheet.
Summer Street junctions at the right edge were not detected (centre just off the sheet).
W Delaware Av to W 4th St, N/S Church, N Laurel Av, N/S Winter, N/S Summer (blocks 14-17, 54, 56, 79, 112-114). 50 ft. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the west-central part of Florence from West Front Street south to West 5th Street, between South Iron Street at the left and South Church Street at the right, with South Eyre Street and South Boulevard crossing the middle. Blocks 6 and 9 at the left hold frame dwellings, and Library Hall stands on the north side of West Front Street. Blocks 43 to 46 between Eyre and Boulevard, and blocks 48, 49, 76 and 77 to the right, hold detached dwellings in a regular pattern, with the First Baptist Church and its parsonage in block 48 at the upper right and a garage with a heated shop in block 44. Blocks 104, 106 and 13 at the left are laid out in four-house company groups, each a cluster of identical double dwellings, along West 3 1/2 Street, which is lettered but is not in OpenStreetMap. St. Paul's Baptist Church stands in block 110 on West 5th Street. A private railroad runs along the 120 foot West 5th Street at the bottom, shown as a pair of curved track lines crossing the sheet from the left to the lower right. South Church Street is lettered as a diagonal street at the right, with the blank blocks 4 and 10 of adjoining sheets beyond it. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inch size and dry hydrants run along the streets, and a scale bar and compass rose are on the sheet. The adjoining sheets are numbered 1, 4, 6 and 10.
notes: South Boulevard is Boulevard Street in OpenStreetMap; the printed South Iron, Eyre and Church are Iron Street, Eyre Street and Church Street.
West 3 1/2 Street has no OpenStreetMap counterpart, so it has no control.
Eyre Street / West 3rd Street was detected but rejected as 13.9 m off the fit.
Rotation of this sheet (about -10.6 degrees) differs from sheets 2, 3 and 4 (about -18 degrees); the streets on the sheet are drawn square to the page.
W Front to W 5th St, S Iron, S Eyre, S Boulevard, S Church (blocks 6, 9, 13, 43-49, 76-77, 104, 106, 110). Private railroad along W 5th St. 50 ft. One part. W 3 1/2 St not in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the south-western edge of old Florence, from West Front Street south to West 5th Street, between the diagonal line of the Florence Pipe Foundry grounds on the left and South Iron Street at the right. South Union Street and South Foundry Street cross the upper part and South Zinc Street the lower right. At the upper left lie blocks 2 and 3, rows of identical double frame dwellings facing 15 foot alleys, bounded on the left by a diagonal West Front Street and by the foundry's block 36, with a stand pipe of 80,000 gallons capacity. In the upper right are blocks 5 and 4 with dwellings, stores, a cement store, a bakery, a pool room and a lodge on or near West 2nd and West 3rd streets, and a small building filled blue near the right edge. Below West 3rd Street, block 10 and the company groups in blocks 103, 105 and 107 face West 3 1/2 Street and West 4th Street. A private railroad runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right across the sheet beside South Bodine Street. South of it, the lower left is the company housing district of the pipe foundry: W. New 3rd to W. New 7th streets are lettered as stubs of lot lines, still largely unbuilt, in block 9. Block 38 and block 109 are empty. The sheet has a scale bar and compass rose, with north to the upper left, and is bordered by sheets 7, 8, 9, 5 and 1.
notes: Printed S. Union, Foundry, Zinc, Iron and Bodine are Union Street, Foundry Street, Zinc Street, Iron Street and Bodine Street in OpenStreetMap; West New 3rd to 7th are West 3rd Street, West 4th Street, West 5th Street, Park Street and West 6th Street.
West 3 1/2 Street is not in OpenStreetMap.
Zinc Street / West 3rd Street was left out: it was 4.2 m off the fit. West Front Street junctions were left out as the drawn street is diagonal or has an uncertain centre.
The bearing of the grid on this sheet (about -10 degrees) differs from sheets 2 to 4.

W Front to W 5th St, S Union, S Foundry, S Zinc, S Iron; S Bodine and the private railroad diagonally across the lower half, W New 3rd to 7th St stubs. 50 ft. One part. Front St junctions and Zinc St left out (diagonal Front, Zinc 4 m off).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 is given over to the main works of the Florence Pipe Foundry and Machine Co., between West Front Street and the Delaware River at the west end of Florence. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north to the right, so West Front Street runs down the left side of the sheet and the river shore along the right. The works fill block 34: the large Main Shop, the Old Foundry, the Hydrant Foundry with its fitting and core rooms, the H. and B. Machine Shop, a second machine shop, pattern storage buildings, a brass foundry, a blacksmith shop, a power house, a rope house, a pipe cutting shed and a proving press near the river, a repair and electric shop, storage rooms, lumber storage and cleaning sheds. Along West Front Street stand the company office, a hospital, a garage and the house of the company's own fire department, whose equipment is described in a note. A long note gives the watchman service, power, heating, sprinklers and the water supply, pumped from the river through suction lines to a tank and standpipe. Railroad sidings sweep in from the pipe storage yard at the top of the sheet and run along the river, with an overhead travelling crane between the shops. At the left edge the ends of South Union and South Foundry streets meet West Front Street, where the street bends; the blocks beyond belong to sheets 6 and 8.
notes: Placed from two junctions on West Front Street (Foundry Street detected, Union Street hand-picked at the bend): a two-point helmert, low confidence; the river side of the works is about 900 ft from control.
Florence Pipe Foundry and Machine Co. works between W Front and the Delaware River; S Foundry and S Union at left. Drawn turned (north to the right). 50 ft. One part; few street junctions.

sheet-8-1.description: Sheet 8 shows the western works of the Florence Pipe Foundry and Machine Co. on the west side of West Front Street, with a block of company housing east of the street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The foundry occupies most of the sheet (block 34): the New Foundry with its ovens and cupola, the Sand Spun Foundry No. 7, a long cleaning shed, the proving press and tarring rooms, a cement lining building, a core room, a pump house, transformers, overhead travelling cranes and a wooden trestle on concrete piers. Railroad sidings fan across the upper left into the pipe storage yard, and six-inch water pipes with hydrants run through the grounds; the company report is referred to sheet 7. East of West Front Street, between South Bodine and South Woodlawn, a row of identical double frame dwellings faces South Richardson Street and West New 3rd Street, and the block between Richardson and Woodlawn holds the company's garages, two long rows of concrete block auto houses. South Woodlawn is lettered 95 feet wide and Richardson as a 20 foot street. A private railroad follows South Bodine along the top of the sheet, where South Union and West 3rd Street meet it at the upper right corner. Block 102, south of Woodlawn, is empty. The lower right corner is an inset of the south end of block 34, placed separately.
notes: West New 3rd St. is West 3rd Street in OpenStreetMap.
South Woodlawn, 95 ft wide, is mapped today as two carriageways named Woodlawn Avenue and Boulevard Street about 15 m apart; the hand-picked control uses the midpoint.
Placed from four hand-picked junctions in the upper right of the sheet; the foundry grounds to the west are far from control.

Florence Pipe Foundry west works and pipe storage yard, W Front, S Bodine, S Richardson, S Woodlawn, W New 3rd St; north to upper left. 50 ft. Part 2: inset at bottom right behind a heavy line (block 34 on W Front).

sheet-8-2.description: This inset in the lower right corner of sheet 8 continues the main map southward beyond the bottom edge of the sheet: it shows the south end of block 34, the Florence Pipe Foundry and Machine Co. grounds, on the west side of West Front Street, at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. At its top it repeats the south end of the foundry building that closes the main map, with the six-inch water pipe along it. Below are a dust house, a row of sheds and a private garage, and two frame dwellings near West Front Street. The edges of the inset are marked no exposure.
notes: Placed by carrying points from part 1: the inset repeats the foundry building and dust house drawn at the bottom of part 1 at the same scale and orientation, offset by +2787, -1545 px. Low confidence.

Florence Pipe Foundry west works and pipe storage yard, W Front, S Bodine, S Richardson, S Woodlawn, W New 3rd St; north to upper left. 50 ft. Part 2: inset at bottom right behind a heavy line (block 34 on W Front).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the pipe foundry's company housing district south-west of Florence, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right. A grid of streets lettered West New 3rd to West New 7th Street crosses it from top to bottom. South Woodlawn at the left is a wide boulevard (95 feet) with large blank blocks beyond it: block 111 holds five pairs of company dwellings in pink and yellow beside a row of lots; blocks 35 and 101 are marked not open. Between South Richardson Street and South Bodine Street lie blocks 37 and 39, each with two rows of identical double frame dwellings facing 20 foot alleys, and blocks 40 and 41 with four company groups of cross-shaped dwellings between West New 5th, 6th and 7th streets. A row of seven dwellings stands on West New 7th Street. A private railroad follows the right edge along South Bodine Street, where South Union and West 3rd Street meet it at the top and South Foundry at the right edge, with six inch water pipes and hydrants. A baseball field with a grand stand is drawn at the bottom right, in block 2, with curved lines of a track or drive along it. The sheet number 9 and a compass rose are at the top right, and block 8 of the adjoining sheet of the foundry works lies at the top. Block 6 is at the right edge.
notes: West New 3rd to 7th are West 3rd Street, West 4th Street, West 5th Street, Park Street and West 6th Street in OpenStreetMap; Richardson, Bodine, Union and Foundry are Richardson Street, Bodine Street, Union Street and Foundry Street.
South Woodlawn is mapped today as two carriageways, Woodlawn Avenue and Boulevard Street, and was not used for control.
Park Street / Richardson Street was detected but excluded (3.8 m off the fit).
The label at the upper right edge reads W. 3RD with the street cut by the crop at full size; read as West 3rd Street.

Company housing: W New 3rd to W New 7th St, S Woodlawn, S Richardson, S Bodine; baseball field. Turned (north to the upper right). 50 ft. One part. Woodlawn (two modern carriageways) not used; W New 6th = Park Street, W New 7th = West 6th Street.

sheet-10-1.description: Sheet 10, part 1, is the upper strip of the sheet, showing two block rows of south-western Florence from West 4th Street south to West 6th Street, between South Winter Street at the centre and South Summer Street at the right edge. The 120 foot West 5th Street crosses the middle, with a private railroad shown as parallel track lines that converge into one at the centre. North of it, blocks 60 at the left and 61 at the right hold scattered frame dwellings, a public school in a pink brick building at the upper left corner, a shed, a milk house and a foundation, with a long block of vacant stores and sheds on the Winter Street frontage. South of West 5th Street blocks 67 and 68 are largely empty, with a few dwellings at the right. A section of South Winter Street between 5th and 6th is lettered as not opened. West 6th Street runs along the bottom, where a heavy line divides this part from the lower part of the sheet. The streets are lettered 60 feet wide, with half-widths of 40 feet at the margins and 20 foot alleys. A compass rose with north toward the upper left stands at the left on the dividing line. The sheet number 10 is printed in the upper corners, and sheets 4, 5 and 3 adjoin.
notes: Printed West 4th to 6th are West 4th Street, West 5th Street and West 6th Street in OpenStreetMap; South Winter and South Summer are Winter Street and Summer Street.
Placed by four hand-picked junctions (Winter and Summer with West 4th and West 6th), measured from block edges and half street widths; no leave-one-out is available.
West 5th Street was left out: the modern junctions are about 6 m from the centre of the drawn 120 foot street, whose line is occupied by the private railroad.

Two parts at 50 ft separated by a heavy line: part 1 (top) W 4th to W 6th St between S Winter and S Summer; part 2 (bottom) W 4th to W 6th St between S Summer and S Spring. Private railroad in W 5th St. Both parts hand-picked (4 points each); W 5th St (railroad in street, modern centre 6-7 m off) left out.

sheet-10-2.description: Sheet 10, part 2, is the lower strip of the sheet, showing blocks of south-western Florence between South Summer Street at the left and South Spring Street at the right, from West 4th Street south to West 6th Street. Blocks 62 and 63 lie just below the heavy dividing line: block 62 at the left holds a few dwellings and a storage shed, and block 63 at the right dwellings and a small building coloured blue near the centre, with a lodge or hall at the right edge. The 120 foot West 5th Street crosses the middle with a private railroad running along it in two long track lines. Below it, block 69 at the left is almost empty except for a dwelling near South Summer Street and another in the lower middle, while block 70 at the right is lined with dwellings along South Spring Street and has a larger building at the lower right. Alleys of 20 feet divide the blocks, and the streets are lettered 60 feet wide at the margins. The upper right corner carries the neighbouring sheet numbers 2 and 1 in the right margin, and a scale bar and copyright note appear at the bottom right. The part is separated from part 1 by a heavy line along the top, running left across the sheet.
notes: Printed South Summer, South Spring and West 4th to 6th are Summer Street, Spring Street and West 4th Street to West 6th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed by four hand-picked junctions (Summer and Spring with West 4th and West 6th) from block edges and half street widths; no leave-one-out is available.
West 5th Street was left out: the modern nodes are about 7 m from the centre of the drawn 120 foot street, which carries a private railroad.

Two parts at 50 ft separated by a heavy line: part 1 (top) W 4th to W 6th St between S Winter and S Summer; part 2 (bottom) W 4th to W 6th St between S Summer and S Spring. Private railroad in W 5th St. Both parts hand-picked (4 points each); W 5th St (railroad in street, modern centre 6-7 m off) left out.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the eastern side of Florence from East Front Street south to East 9th Street, between South Chestnut Street at the left and the edge near South Pine Street at the right, with South Walnut and South Spruce streets between. The upper left holds the older residential blocks 27 to 29, 57 to 59 and 65, 66, each ruled into lots with frame dwellings; St. Clare Church (Roman Catholic) stands at the upper left on East Front Street, and Emmon's Laundry, with its power and steam plant, stands in block 128 at the upper right, beside a greenhouse. Blocks 128, 131 and 134 to the right are largely open land. The 120 foot East 5th Street carries a private railroad that curves from the left edge and runs diagonally to the lower right. South of it are blocks 32, 71, 75 and 33 with scattered dwellings, large open blocks 81 and 126, and at the lower right the small blocks 138 to 141 cut by the oblique line of South Cedar Lane. Block numbers 125, 127 and 142 are at the bottom edge. A scale bar and compass rose are included, with north toward the upper right. The streets are lettered 60 feet wide, the alleys 20 feet, and the adjoining sheets are numbered 2, 1 and 10.
notes: East 7th Street is Wilbur Henry Drive in OpenStreetMap; South Chestnut, Walnut, Spruce and Pine are Chestnut Street, Walnut Street, Spruce Street and Pine Street.
South Cedar Lane is Cedar Lane in OpenStreetMap; it was not used for control.

sheet-12-1.description: The main part of sheet 12 shows Florence Station, the railroad settlement about one and a half miles southeast of the Florence post office, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division crosses the sheet from left to right, with the passenger station (Florence Station) and a freight station beside the tracks, and Railroad Avenue running along their north side. Delaware Avenue, marked one and a half miles to Florence, crosses the tracks near the middle of the sheet; Cow Lane runs diagonally across it on both sides of the railroad, and Hamilton Avenue leaves Delaware Avenue eastward in the lower right. Blocks 202 to 207 are mostly frame dwellings with private garages, sheds and chicken coops, with large open lots. On Delaware Avenue south of the tracks stand the fire house of the Florence Volunteer Fire Company No. 2 and a public garage with a gasoline tank. Two areas of the sheet, set off by heavy lines at the upper left and lower left, are insets of other blocks and are georeferenced separately. Much of the frontage is marked no exposure along the sheet edges, and lot and house numbers are given along Delaware Avenue and Railroad Avenue.
notes: Cow Lane does not match a modern street: today's Station Road crosses Delaware Avenue at the railroad on a different line, so it was not used for control.
Railroad is the River Line in OpenStreetMap (P.R.R. Amboy Division on the sheet).
The 20 ft alley north of Hamilton Avenue east of Delaware Avenue matches Tilton Lane.

sheet-12-2.description: This inset in the upper left corner of sheet 12 shows the north side of Railroad Avenue at 5th Avenue, west of the blocks on the main part of the sheet, at Florence Station. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the same orientation as the main map, north toward the upper right. Block 201, west of 5th Avenue, holds a long row of private garages, a few dwellings and a grain and feed building facing Railroad Avenue, with a short siding curving off the railroad toward it. East of 5th Avenue a corner of block 202 is drawn, almost empty apart from a small building at its edge. Fifth Avenue is lettered with a width of 87 feet. The edges toward the top are marked no exposure. Lot numbers 6 to 14 are given along Railroad Avenue.
notes: 5th Av is no longer a street; its 84 ft right-of-way survives as a gap in today's parcels about 277 m southwest of Delaware Avenue along Railroad Avenue, which was used to place the inset.

sheet-12-3.description: This inset in the lower left of sheet 12 shows Delaware Avenue between Wallace Avenue and Burlington Pike at Florence Station, south of the blocks on the main part of the sheet. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, like the main map. Blocks 206, 208 and 209 line Delaware Avenue with frame dwellings, private garages, a feed house and two public garages, one of concrete block with a capacity of 15 cars, with gasoline tanks along Burlington Pike. A 20 foot alley crosses Wallace Avenue east of Delaware Avenue. Burlington Pike, 68 feet wide, runs along the bottom edge with only its north side drawn. The east and west edges of the inset are marked no exposure.
notes: The alley east of Delaware Avenue across Wallace Avenue matches Tilton Alley.

Burlington Pike at Delaware Avenue is today the junction with Burlington-Bordentown Road (US 130) and Florence-Columbus Road; the pike centre was hand-placed half its lettered 68 ft width beyond the drawn edge.
